stories.situation: As a founder, there is no escalation path — every infrastructure decision, outage, and security call terminates with you.
stories.task: Design, build, secure, and operate production systems end-to-end with no team to hide behind.
stories.action: I built and operated the full stack: infrastructure, CI/CD pipelines, security controls, and production operations — learning each layer by owning its failures, not by reading about them.
stories.result: I developed the exact muscle this role needs: end-to-end ownership, systematic troubleshooting, and the habit of documenting everything because future-me is the on-call engineer.
stories.honestyNote: Founder is the title; the work was real. Don't inflate team size or revenue.

stories.title: The homelab migration
stories.basedOn: Homelab infrastructure work: RAID 0 (E:) data migration, Proton pipeline operations, Hyper-V/VM builds (documented across his projects).
stories.situation: My homelab outgrew its storage layout and I needed to migrate live data to a new RAID 0 array without losing anything.
stories.task: Plan and execute a storage migration with zero data loss and minimal service interruption.
stories.action: I verified backups first, built the array, migrated in staged batches with checksum verification, and validated every service after cutover — treating it with production change discipline.
stories.result: Clean migration, zero data loss, and a reusable runbook. It's also why I can whiteboard a VM build or a migration plan on demand — I've done the reps.
stories.honestyNote: Homelab scale, stated plainly — interviewers respect honest homelab depth.

stories.title: Shipping the knowledge platform
stories.basedOn: Built and deployed interstitiumlabs.dev / learn.interstitiumlabs.dev to production (documented).
stories.situation: I set out to build a production-grade knowledge platform — not a demo, a real deployed system.
stories.task: Ship enterprise-grade quality: no broken links, no half-finished pages, verified before every deploy.
stories.action: I built automated verification gates — link integrity, content validity, production readiness — into the deploy process, so nothing ships broken. Every deploy is verified, not hoped.
stories.result: A live production platform maintained to that bar continuously. That 'verify before you ship' discipline is exactly how I'd treat infrastructure changes here.
stories.honestyNote: Real shipped product. The quality-gate habit is the transferable point.

stories.title: The honest junior
stories.basedOn: His stated positioning: junior candidate aiming to earn senior-level capability; ThreatLocker's reported openness to cybersecurity career-starters.
stories.situation: I'm interviewing as a junior infrastructure candidate against people with more years on paper.
stories.task: Make the honest case for trajectory over tenure.
stories.action: I've spent months in focused, verifiable preparation — bootcamp enrollment, certification-track study across A+, Network+, Security+, and Windows Server, and hands-on homelab reps. I learn systems end-to-end and document everything.
stories.result: I'm not asking anyone to pretend I'm senior. I'm asking to be evaluated on trajectory, preparation, and how fast I close gaps — and this interview itself is the evidence.
stories.honestyNote: Never apologize for being junior; sell the slope, not the intercept.

cards.back: Situation (context) → Task (your responsibility) → Action (what YOU did, specifically) → Result (outcome + lesson). Under two minutes. End on the lesson.

cards.front: The honesty tripwires — what never to say
cards.back: Never 'completed' the bootcamp (enrolled Sept 30). Never invent employers, metrics, or team sizes. Never claim certifications you don't hold. If pressed, say 'I don't have that yet — here's what I do have.'

notes: Rehearsal method: record each story, listen back, cut filler. Two minutes max per story.
Every story must end with the lesson or the transferable skill — that's what interviewers remember.

quiz.q: An interviewer asks about the bootcamp. Which answer holds the honesty line?
choices: 'I enrolled September 30th and have been working through the Zero Trust material since — here's what I took from the default-deny model...'
quiz.explain: Enrolled + substance beats false completion every time — and they can verify.

fastTrackModules.title: Mock interview module — timed and scored
objectives: Complete four timed mock rounds and score at least 70% on each.
Rehearse the demo-presentation format ThreatLocker publicly described.
Convert every sub-70% round into a targeted re-take the same day.
fastTrackModules.summary: Four timed, scored mock rounds modeled on the interview structure ThreatLocker publicly described for an IT-adjacent role (technical phone screen → demo presentation → onsite troubleshooting), plus a behavioral round. Framing is honest: the Infrastructure Specialist loop may differ — prepare for all formats.
fastTrackModules.formatFraming: ThreatLocker publicly described a three-step process for its Senior Technical Support Specialist role: (1) technical phone interview, (2) product demo presentation back to the team, (3) onsite hands-on troubleshooting session. This mock mirrors that structure with a behavioral round added. The IT Infrastructure Specialist loop may differ.

rounds.title: Technical phone screen
rounds.source: Sample 8 from FT02 (mix reported + likely); answer aloud, 90 seconds each.
rounds.scoring: 0-3 per question: 0 wrong/silent, 1 vague, 2 correct, 3 correct + evidence. Pass: >=17/24.

rounds.title: Demo presentation
rounds.source: Prepare and deliver a 10-minute whiteboard talk: 'How I would harden and document a new Windows Server for a Zero Trust environment.' Then 20 minutes of follow-up questions from FT02.
rounds.scoring: Clarity 0-6, technical accuracy 0-6, handling questions 0-6, time discipline 0-6. Pass: >=17/24.

rounds.title: Onsite troubleshooting simulation
rounds.source: Three scenarios, 10 minutes each, thinking aloud: (a) user can't reach the file share; (b) GPO not applying; (c) VM lost network after a change. Narrate the methodology, not just the answer.
rounds.scoring: Methodology 0-4, correct diagnosis 0-4, communication 0-4 per scenario. Pass: >=25/36.

rounds.title: Behavioral and fit
rounds.source: FT02 Behavioral slice: deliver 3 STAR stories plus 'why ThreatLocker' and 'why hire you'.
rounds.scoring: 0-3 per answer: structure, honesty, evidence. Pass: >=11/15.

fastTrackModules.overallRule: Overall pass: all four rounds at or above their pass marks. Any round below → targeted study of its weakest questions → re-take the same day.

cards.front: Thinking aloud — the meta-skill of round 3
cards.back: Narrate: 'I'm checking X first because...'. Interviewers score the methodology they can hear, not the answer you reach silently.
They're scoring communication clarity as much as technical depth. Structure: problem → approach → demo → trade-offs → questions. Finish early rather than ramble.

notes: Do rounds 1-4 back-to-back on Day 5 to simulate interview fatigue.
Record audio of every round. The playback reveals filler, hedging, and rambling you can't hear live.

fastTrackModules.title: Day-before and day-of checklist
objectives: Arrive composed, early, and fully prepared on Tue Oct 13, 9:00 AM ET.
Verify the interview location from the invitation before traveling.
Carry everything needed: documents, proof of preparation, and calm.
fastTrackModules.summary: Logistics win interviews before they start. Day-before preparation and a minute-by-minute day-of timeline for the October 13, 9:00 AM ET interview.
fastTrackModules.locationNote: Plan anchor: 1950 W Maitland Blvd, Orlando (per the interview invitation details provided). VERIFY against your invitation email before traveling — ThreatLocker's public listings show its headquarters at 1950 Summit Park Drive, Orlando, FL 32810, so confirm which address your interview uses.
dayBefore: Confirm the interview address from the invitation email (see location note above). Map the route and drive it if possible.
Print 5 copies of your resume on clean paper; prepare a one-page portfolio summary (homelab builds, bootcamp enrollment, cert track).
Lay out professional attire; pack bag: resumes, portfolio summary, notebook + pen, photo ID, references list, phone charger, water.
Review the 9 reported questions and your 6 STAR stories once — lightly. No cramming after 8 PM.
Set two alarms. Target sleep by 10:30 PM.
dayOf: 6:30 AM — wake, no snooze. Protein breakfast; no excess caffeine.
7:00 AM — final review: 60-second 'why ThreatLocker', VM-build walkthrough, one STAR story. Then stop studying.
7:45 AM — depart with 30+ minutes buffer. Account for Orlando morning traffic.
8:35-8:40 AM — arrive. Check in calmly; breathe; review your one-page cheat sheet once, then put it away.
9:00 AM — interview. Think aloud, anchor answers to real experience, hold the honesty line.
After — send a brief thank-you note referencing something specific from the conversation.
fastTrackModules.screeningNote: ThreatLocker's publicly posted roles describe a background check and drug/substance screening after a conditional offer. Keep a valid photo ID ready and expect this step — it is their standard process, not a surprise.

cards.back: Arrive → breathe (4 counts in, 6 out, 3 rounds) → recall one STAR story → remind yourself: 'trajectory, preparation, honesty' → walk in.

cards.front: If you don't know an answer
cards.back: 'I haven't hit that in production yet. Here's how I'd figure it out: [method].' Honesty + method beats bluffing every time — bluffing is detectable and fatal.

notes: Eat before you go. Low blood sugar ruins more interviews than hard questions.
Phone on silent before entering the building, not after sitting down.

fastTrackModules.title: Offer and onboarding readiness
objectives: Evaluate an offer calmly against your criteria.
Complete post-offer screening steps without friction.
Arrive on day one with a 30/60/90 plan.
fastTrackModules.summary: No hiring promise is made or implied — this module prepares you to handle an offer professionally if one comes: evaluation, screening, and a first-90-days plan that shows you're already thinking like an owner.
offerEvaluation: Compare total compensation, not just salary: benefits, growth path, and the value of the experience itself.
Confirm role scope in writing: title, team, primary responsibilities, on-call expectations.
Ask about the certification and training support — it signals a growth culture and funds your AZ/Security+ path.
Take the full decision window; never accept on the spot from excitement.
screeningPrep: Background check and drug/substance screening follow a conditional offer per their public postings — keep ID and documentation ready.
Ensure your references are warned and reachable.
Keep your documented history consistent with what you stated in interviews.
first90Plan: Days 1-30: learn — document the environment as you discover it; ask questions; complete compliance and tooling onboarding; shadow escalations.
Days 31-60: contribute — own L2 tickets end-to-end; propose one documentation improvement; start the first certification (Security+).
Days 61-90: lead — own a small infrastructure improvement; present a lunch-and-learn on something you learned; have AZ-800 booked.

cards.back: 30: learn the environment and document it. 60: contribute independently and start certifying. 90: lead something small and teach something back.

notes: Write the 30/60/90 on one page and bring it if a final-round conversation invites it — unprompted is fine only if the moment fits.

studyGuide.title: IL-27 study guide: how to work this course
studyGuide.framing: Independent certification preparation. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by CompTIA, Microsoft, or ThreatLocker.

plan: Phase 1 — Foundations, M01-M06 (~72 h, ~3 weeks): A+ track. Hardware on the bench, OS in VMs, triage methodology drilled daily. Gate: gate-aplus.
Phase 2 — Networking, M07-M10 (~48 h, ~2 weeks): subnet to automaticity, build the SOHO/branch lab, run network triage scenarios. Gate: gate-netplus.
Phase 3 — Security + Zero Trust, M11-M14 (~48 h, ~2 weeks): threats, architecture, operations, and the Zero Trust domain. Gate: gate-secplus.
Phase 4 — Windows Server hybrid core, M15-M18 (~48 h, ~2 weeks): build a domain from scratch, Hyper-V lab, storage and hybrid networking. Gate: gate-az800.
Phase 5 — Windows Server advanced, M19-M21 (~36 h, ~1.5 weeks): hardening baselines, HA/DR planning, migration and monitoring. Gate: gate-az801.
Phase 6 — Endpoint + capstone, M22-M24 (~36 h, ~1.5 weeks): deployment, identity/compliance, app lifecycle, capstone portfolio assembly. Gate: gate-md102.
Phase 7 — Certification gates: sit practice gates in the exam order below; book each real exam only when the dashboard reads READY TO SIT (>=85%).
pacing.note: 240 minutes a day, 6 days a week, completes the full CBT in about 12 weeks. The 6-day interview fast track (IL27-FT01..FT06) runs in parallel or standalone ahead of 2026-10-13. Slower is fine — the dashboard measures readiness, not speed.

whenStuck.title: When you are stuck (exact remediation path)
steps: 1. Re-check: re-read the module note that introduced the concept and re-run its worked example by hand. Most blocks are a skipped prerequisite.
2. Drills: work the module drill set until every item is correct twice in a row. If a drill item confuses you, that is the exact gap — name it.
3. Labs: rebuild the lab from scratch instead of re-reading. Infrastructure knowledge lives in the hands, not the eyes.
4. Cross-links: follow the module crossLinks — the concept is rebuilt from a different angle there (e.g., triage methodology in M04, M10, and M21).
5. Teach it: explain the concept aloud as if to the interviewer. Whatever you cannot say plainly, you do not know yet.

examOrder.title: Recommended certification exam order
examOrder.rule: Sit a practice gate only when that exam's dashboard row is at least NEARLY READY (70%). Book the real exam only when it reads READY TO SIT (85%) on the 60%-modules / 40%-gate formula — and only after scoring >=80% on the gate twice.

order.why: Broadest foundation; every later track assumes its hardware, OS, and troubleshooting vocabulary.
Builds directly on A+ networking; required context for hybrid and security work.
Builds on A+ and Network+; the Zero Trust domain here is the interview's conceptual core.
Endpoint administration before server administration — smaller blast radius while learning.

order.cert: Microsoft AZ-800: Administering Windows Server Hybrid Core Infrastructure
order.why: Core server infrastructure; AZ-801 assumes this knowledge.

order.cert: Microsoft AZ-801: Configuring Windows Server Hybrid Advanced Services
order.why: Advanced capstone of the server track; sit last when the full picture is assembled.

studyGuide.timeFormula: total_minutes = sum(module estimatedMinutes) + sum(gate minutes x attempts); weeks = total_minutes / (dailyMinutes x daysPerWeek). At 240 min/day x 6 days/week, 17,280 minutes = 12 weeks. Interview fast track: 6 days at ~240 min/day (day 5: 300, day 6: 120).

dossier.title: IL-27 Graduate Evidence Map — printable dossier
dossier.framing: Independent preparation record. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by CompTIA, Microsoft, or ThreatLocker. Record only work you actually completed and scores you actually earned — this dossier is evidence, not aspiration.

sections.heading: How to use this dossier
sections.intro: Print this map and fill it as you finish the course. Each row connects a certification domain to the modules that teach it, the gate that tests it, the score you earned, and the portfolio artifact that proves it. In interviews, each row is a talking point with receipts.
bullets: Complete a module only when its labs and drills are green — then tick it off.
Record every gate attempt with date and score; the dashboard uses your BEST score.
Build every portfolio artifact from your own lab work — never download someone else's.
Bring the filled map to interviews: it turns 'I studied' into 'here's the evidence.'
